key_insight: Qurrium is a Qiskit-based Python package that makes randomized-measurement methods, especially classical shadows, practical for estimating key quantum state properties from either simulated or hardware-collected data.
engineering_relevance: It lowers the tooling barrier for quantum hardware benchmarking and many-body state analysis by providing an end-to-end and a standalone analysis workflow in a widely used software stack.
method: Implements randomized measurement protocols for purity, second-order Rényi entropy, Pauli expectations, and state overlap.
Supports an end-to-end workflow from circuit preparation and simulation to measurement and analysis.
Supports a standalone workflow that ingests pre-collected measurement data from compatible hardware platforms.
evidence_signal: The paper demonstrates the package on cluster-state and Ising time-evolved-state examples and reports analysis results from a superconducting quantum processor.
watch_item: Results depend on the quality and format of measurement data, so the standalone workflow requires careful hardware-data compatibility and consistent preprocessing.
paper_title: Qurrium: A Python package for randomized measurement-based estimation of quantum state properties
